title: Bag fee is missing
doc: bag_fee(bags) must return 0 when the customer brought their own bag (bags is 0) and 1 when they need a bag (bags is 1). Right now customers who need a bag are not charged.

glossary.==: Checks whether two things are equal.
glossary.if: Runs the next block only when the condition is true.

line_notes.1: That line just names the function, so it can't be the problem.
line_notes.2: That line checks whether the customer brought a bag. The check itself is fine.
line_notes.3: That's the answer for customers with their own bag, who pay nothing. That part is right.
line_notes.4: That line only starts the “otherwise” branch.
line_notes.6: That bracket just closes the branch.
line_notes.7: That bracket just closes the function.

hints: Think about who should pay for a bag, then look at what each branch of the code gives back.
Look at the “otherwise” branch. That's the customer who needs a bag. Does it return what the description says?
tutorial.right_why: A customer who needs a bag should pay 1, so the “otherwise” branch has to return 1 instead of 0.

option_notes.b: That charges 2, but the description says 1.
option_notes.c: “charge” isn't defined anywhere, so the app would crash.
option_notes.d: That gives 1 too, but it's a clumsy way to write it.
